questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The most crucial thing for me was to visit an English speaking country so that I could better my legal English skills. Furthermore, I wanted to choose a university that valued diversity and social well being for the students, which UoN definitely provided.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: For UoN, they really do take you by the hand and help you each step of the way. At no point of my arrival did I feel lost or uncertain. I knew where I had to be and when. They also send mails out frequently that explained where we could find the information needed to keep up with our schedule and etc.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I didn't receive any additional assistance.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Thankfully UoN have a lot of options when it comes to housing. I just applied through the uni portal and got an offer for my accommodation. If you choose to find it yourself, it won't be hard, because Nottingham has a ray of students housing to choose from.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: I lived by the city center which was a big advantage for me, especially when having to meet up with friends. Most of the action and the events happen in the city, so it is also easy to get home after a long day or night out with friends. Though if you are sensitive to noise you should be mindful, because living in the city also comes with hearing all the young students that go out on Wednesdays, Thursdays, Fridays and Saturdays.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: When choosing housing please do consider carefully if you want to stay in a catered hall or not. My hall was not catered which was not a problem for me, because I like cooking (I also had my own little kitchen). But some of my friends that stayed in catered halls said it's fine, the food is okay, and it is a cheap option. It all depends on if you want to cook for yourself or if you want hall food (it isn't always the best, so again, be mindfull)

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: UoN has its own portal and they send you a thorough description of how you register into both the institution and also the modules that you want to take. On their website, they also have a step by step guide of how to fill out everything and what documents you should have ready for registration.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: You could always contact IT or the exchange students center.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Very succesful, I got all the classes that I wanted. But you have to be fast when it comes to registering for the modules because they work with the first come first serve principle.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Just read all the emails and the guides that they give you. Then breathe and take it a step at a time.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I took all level 4 courses and my contact person/adviser from UoN did warn me that the classes may be a bit hard. I did not feel that way. The classes were easy enough to follow, even with a background in Danish law. It really did help that I have gotten my LL.B. already because now I know how law works and which methods to use when studying. There is still some adjusting to do but nothing that is too bad.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Because I am an LL.M. student I only had seminars, which differs from my experience that I had at UCPH in my undergraduate. I did though like how the professor engage with the students and don't give us too many readings for the class but rather explain the topic of the day and lets us use the knowledge that we have gained on an issue that the professor has written on our study page the week or day before.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Fundamental Principles of Business and Commercial Law, Private International Law of Intellectual Property and International Investment Law.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend all of them.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Cost for trips that I took with the uni - Trips to local cities around England

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Everything is less expensive than here in Denmark. Groceries and just personal goods especially.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: UoN has a lot of societies and I joined at least 4 while I was there. All societies, if they aren't catered to a specific degree, are a mix of people from every faculty at UoN which I thoroughly enjoyed and is a nice change from UCPH.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I took dance, ice skating and also did some travelling with the travel society

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Do some type of sport!! I cannot stress this enough. It is the best way to meet new people.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: If you can visit the different cities around England, then do it. A lot of my friends also went to Scotland or Belfast, because it is easily accessible.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Fairly easy.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Be open, smile and say "Hi, where are you from? What do you study?" This always starts a good conversation.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Mostly the very specific saying that they have in Nottinghamshire county. Things like "tea" being dinner or "ey, up!" meaning hello.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: How open and non-judgemental everyone is.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Be open, be kind and say yes to all opportunities

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Arrive a couple of days before school starts because it gives you time to explore the city you live in now. Also, walk around one day with google maps to help you and see if you can memorise some things. I did this and after a week and a half I could find my way around the city without any form of help and also knew what busses would take me where.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Meeting the most amazing friend group and experiencing life with them.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Adjusting to everyday life in another country alone - But it also made me grow personally and academically.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
